summary: Concurrent function-calls can be applied out-of-order after cross-region retry and batching - leads to inconsistent external side-effects
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when their orchestration issues multiple function-calls (tool calls) in parallel from different regional clients, retries and server-side batching can cause the calls to be applied out-of-order at the downstream webhook. Impact: In a chat orchestration where calls represent financial operations (authorizations -> capture), out-of-order application produced a capture before the authorization for ~0.7% of requests during a high-retry window, causing failed reconciliation and manual refunds. Environment: Enterprise dedicated customer using SDKs in three services: Python v1.2.0 (orchestrator), Typescript v1.3.4 (frontend gateway), Go v1.1.8 (worker). Traffic through prod us-west and eu-west. Steps to reproduce, logs and minimal repro are included below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy three clients: python orchestration service performs two sequential funcalls per logical user action: POST /authorize -> POST /capture (function-calling to external webhook).

2) Simultaneously invoke 50 requests that the orchestrator parallelizes across 5 worker goroutines (Go workers use SDK streaming to dispatch first call), and intentionally drop ACK for 10% of streaming chunks to force retries from the edge.
3) On server side enable default batching (server automatically batches 10-20 requests per RT window).
4) Trigger transient error on api-gateway between us-west and eu-west (5xx for 1.5s) to cause cross-region fallback and retries.
5) Verify downstream webhook sequence numbers for authorize/capture pair; observe capture events arriving before authorize for a subset.

comments: 2026-03-12 - EdgeChat support rep (Elena Morales): Customer reports 0.7% of transactions failing reconciliation. They attached webhook logs with sequence numbers showing capture before authorize. They requested immediate mitigation and guidance for SDK patterns to prevent out-of-order side-effects.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Assigned to engineering, provided short-term mitigation: recommend per-action idempotency tokens and explicit causal ordering in orchestration (block on authorize success before scheduling capture). Also suggested temporarily disabling server-side batching via per-request header x-rw-batching: off for critical flows.

2026-03-12 - Marco Nguyen (Eng): Investigating whether batching reorders events when retries merge cross-region. Hypothesis: when an earlier call is retried later and lands in a different batch, the final batch order is based on arrival timestamp and not original logical sequence. Investigating dedupe/timestamp metadata on batched dispatch.

2026-03-13 - EdgeChat (customer): Implemented per-action idempotency tokens and saw immediate drop in reconciliation errors to <0.01% in a small canary. They requested a platform-level change to preserve per-request causal order or expose ordering guarantees for function-calls.
2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen (Eng): Confirmed reproducer in staging; working on design doc for preserving 'logical sequence' metadata through batching and retry path (internal RFC).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Server-side batching is assigning dispatch order purely by batch arrival timestamp. When a retry from an earlier logical call arrives later, it enters a subsequent batch and is dispatched after later calls that were not retried.

Hypothesis 2: Some SDKs (TS v1.3.4) normalize idempotency tokens by truncation of long UUIDs, causing token collision and unexpected dedupe behavior that can hide replays — NOT primary cause for ordering but noted.

Findings: Reproducer run with verbose trace shows batch_id and per-call original_sequence metadata available in logs but not used when computing dispatch order. Batching code uses wall-clock enqueue timestamp only.

Reproducer: Added custom header x-rw-original-seq to outgoing funcalls in staging; batch dispatcher ignored header when sorting batch members. Patch locally shows reordering when dispatcher sorted by original_sequence instead of arrival timestamp.

Risk: Changing dispatcher sort order to honor original_sequence requires carrying that metadata for all requests (hosted + private) and validating across cross-region failover path; possible increased memory overhead in dispatcher and potential latency impact on throughput.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-12): Support instructed customer to set x-rw-batching: off for critical payment flows and to use explicit per-action idempotency tokens. Customer confirms reduction in incorrect ordering.

Medium-term engineering plan: implement 'preserve_logical_order' flag on function-calling API. When enabled, server will persist original_sequence metadata and prioritize it when assembling dispatch order across retry/batch boundaries. Initial RFC approved 2026-03-13.
SDK changes: Add opt-in helpers in SDKs to surface and consistently propagate an 'original_sequence' header and to avoid token normalization (TS SDK patch PR #118 prevents token truncation).

Planned release: Runtime patch to dispatcher (no user-visible API change) targeted for 2026-03-22 with rollout to non-bursting tenants first. SDK patches to be released: python 1.2.3, ts 1.3.5, go 1.1.9. Documentation update and runbook created in Confluence.

Permanent recommendation for customers with stateful side-effects: always model dependent function-calls as explicit ordered transactions (ack on success then schedule next), or enable preserve_logical_order for batched flows once available.
